summary: This bill amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to treat food as misbranded if its actual nutrient content exceeds the labeled value by more than 5 percent and requires the FDA to update its nutrition labeling regulations within 60 days.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends FDA labeling rules for nutrient accuracy but contains no provisions authorizing, expanding, or reducing federal expenditures. Any enforcement costs would be incidental and minimal.
No tax provisions, rate changes, credits, or revenue measures appear in the bill text.

The bill updates nutrition labeling requirements under the FD&C Act. While nutrition information can indirectly relate to health, the legislation does not address insurance coverage, provider reimbursement, public programs, or market structure of healthcare delivery.
The bill addresses only food labeling and has no connection to firearms, ammunition, or gun regulations.
